sentences.text:
Rishu Masih vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 September,
2024
 Neutral Citation No. 2024:Mphc-Jbp:45852
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pramod Kumar Agrawal

On The 11th Of September, 2024
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 35499 of 2024
 Rishu Masih
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Manish Datt - Senior Advocate with Shri Manish Tiwari 
 applicant.
 Shri C.M. Tiwari - Government Advocate for State
 Shri J.K. Awasthi - Advocate for respondent No.2.
 Order

This is the second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 482 of BNNS for grant of anticipatory bail relating to Crime No.113/2024 registered at Police Station Omti, District Jabalpur (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 406, 409, 120-B/34 of IPC.
Previous anticipatory bail application was dismissed as withdrawn.

2. The case of prosecution in short, is that on 14.03.2024 complainant made a written complaint before the police alleging that he had purchased four wheeler and accused persons fraudulently took the four wheeler of the complainant then accused persons did not return his car.
Later on, he came to know that the accused persons are habitual in such type of activities.
FIR was registered.

3. Learned Senior Advocate for the applicant submits that applicant is NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:45852 2 MCRC-35499-2024 innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is submitted that the present applicant is not the main accused.
In FIR, it is not mentioned that vehicle has been entrusted to the present applicant.
Rent agreement was executed between Piyush Naidu and Rameshwar and in this agreement name of the present applicant is not mentioned.
In memorandum, name of the present applicant is not mentioned.
Present applicant cannot be held responsible on the doctrine of vicarious liability.

Ingredients of Sections 406, 409,
420 of IPC is not available against the applicant.
No evidence is there to establish the offence and therefore no case is made out for the applicant.
Further, two offences cannot coexist simultaneously in the same set of facts.

In support of his contention, reliance has been placed in the case of Delhi Rishu Masih vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106681213/
1 Race Club (1940) Ltd. and Others Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Another reported in 2024 SCC OnLine SC 2248.

sentences.text: It has been prayed that the applicant may be granted anticipatory bail.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State as well as objector have opposed the bail application on the ground that complainant had been lured by the applicant and other co-accused persons to purchase four wheeler and then handover to them by way of rent agreement and thereafter they did not return the said vehicle.
In FIR, name of the present applicant is mentioned and it is also mentioned that applicant has actively participated in this crime.

It is further submitted that other victims namely, Satendra Singh Thakur, Devendra Kumar Kachhi, Shubham Karosiya,
Ravendra Kumar Namdeo, Aman Singh and Rameshwar Kasauriya have also stated in their statements that present applicant is also involved in the crime and; applicant NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:45852 3 MCRC-35499-2024 and other co-accused persons have fraudulently took their vehicles.
He is one of the main accused persons.
Applicant and other co-accused are habitual in such type of activities.

There is one criminal record of the applicant bearing Crime No.406/2020 registered at Police Station Tilwara, District Jabalpur (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 294, 376, 376(2)
(n), 506 of IPC.
Custodial interrogation is required from the applicant in this case.
In view of the above, anticipatory bail may not be granted to the applicant.
5. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case and looking to the seriousness of offence, I am not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the present applicant.
6. Accordingly, the application stands dismissed.

(PRAMOD KUMAR AGRAWAL) JUDGE shahina Rishu Masih vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106681213/
